title: Hiring Decision Archive and Debiasing Protocol
author: Priya Kaur
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the standard process for recording, storing, reviewing, and auditing hiring decisions at Redwood Inference. It combines a lightweight, searchable decision archive with a set of operational controls designed to reduce bias in hiring and preserve legally defensible evidence of decision rationale.

Scope: Applies to all full-time, part-time, and contractor hiring processes across engineering, product, sales, and support. Does not replace legal counsel for sensitive cases (EO/ADA/immigration).

Principles
- Evidence-first: Record the facts and artifacts that drove the decision (scorecards, code tests, de-identified interview notes).
- Minimal personally-identifying exposure: Archive stores redacted PII and links to controlled ATS artifacts.
- Auditability: Every hire/reject decision must be traceable to an owner, panel, and set of artifacts within 7 business days of decision.
- Continuous improvement: Use archived decisions to feed quarterly calibration and debiasing reviews.

Definitions
- Decision record: The canonical JSON/YAML-style object stored in the hiring archive describing outcome, rationale, and ownership.
- Panel owner: The individual responsible for running the interview loop and submitting the final record (usually hiring manager or designated IC).
- Debiasing checkpoint: A discrete review step triggered for final-stage candidates with elevated risk factors (e.g., low panel consensus, demographic signal outside expected distribution).

Process overview (high level)
1) Panel concludes interviews and completes final scorecard in Greenhouse (or ATS of record).
2) Panel owner creates the Decision record in the Hiring Archive Confluence form within 72 hours.
3) People Ops automation validates required fields, strips PII where specified, and attaches canonical references (ATS id, Workday placeholder, evaluation artifacts stored in secure artifact store).
4) If a Debiasing Checkpoint is triggered, People Ops schedules a 30-minute panel calibration call within 5 business days.
5) Records are retained per retention policy and surfaced to quarterly calibration audits.

Panel preparation checklist (before closing loop)
- Confirm panel composition meets panel-equity guidance (>=2 interviewers, at least one interviewer from outside immediate team for non-senior roles).
- Ensure interview rubrics are the current version (link: /confluence/people-ops/interview-rubrics).
- Notify People Ops that candidate is being advanced to final review (Slack: #hiring-ops).

Step-by-step recording procedure
1. Finalize scorecards in ATS and export the aggregated score summary (CSV or PDF).
2. Open the Hiring Archive Confluence form (Create -> Hiring Decision Record).
3. Populate the canonical fields (see "Decision record template" below).
4. Upload redacted interview notes. Redaction rules: remove PII (email, phone, address) and medical/immigration comments; leave behavioral and technical content intact.
5. Select the Debiasing Checkpoint flag if any of these are true: panel disagreement > 2 points, candidate changed role after referral, marked counter-offer risk, or candidate demographic falls into underrepresented group for the role.
6. Submit. Automation validates and returns a unique decision-id (format: RDW-HIR-YYYYNNNN).

Decision record template (fields required)
- decision_id: unique id (assigned on submit)
- candidate_alias: initials + numeric suffix (redacted)
- role_id: internal role code
- team: hiring team name (string)
- outcome: hire | no-hire | hold | withdraw
- decision_date: YYYY-MM-DD
- panel_owner: name and email (email is stored in secured metadata, redacted in public archive view)
- interview_panel: list of interviewer names (public view shows names only)
- score_summary: brief numeric summary and rubric version (e.g., 3.8/5 — rubric v2.4)
- primary_rationale: short-form reason (30–200 words)
- evidence_links: list of links (ATS scorecard, code test url, recorded assignment)
- redaction_compliance: yes|no (did submitter follow redaction rules?)
- debiasing_flag: yes|no
- closed_by: name and role of approver (if different from panel_owner)
- legal_hold: yes|no (if legal counsel flagged case)

Decision archive schema example (for operational teams)
Note: archive stores a single-line JSON string per record in the secure artifact store. This example is for illustration and should not be copy-pasted into public channels.

{
  "decision_id": "RDW-HIR-20290042",
  "candidate_alias": "PK-42",
  "role_id": "ENG-REQ-321",
  "team": "serving-runtime",
  "outcome": "no-hire",
  "decision_date": "2028-11-10",
  "panel_owner": "Ava Martinez",
  "interview_panel": ["Ava Martinez","David Chen","Lila Thompson"],
  "score_summary": "2.8/5 — rubric v2.3",
  "primary_rationale": "Candidate performed well on systems design but did not meet the coding rubric threshold for the role.\",
  "evidence_links": ["greenhouse://scorecard/12345","s3://redacted-artifacts/eng-321/code-test-42.zip"],
  "redaction_compliance": "yes",
  "debiasing_flag": "no",
  "closed_by": "Ava Martinez",
  "legal_hold": "no"
}

Retention, access, and security
- Short-term: decision records are visible to panel members and People Ops for 18 months. Public Confluence view exposes redacted fields only.
- Long-term: after 18 months, records are moved to secure, read-only cold storage (encrypted S3 bucket) for an additional 3 years for audit and compliance needs.
- Access control: People Ops and People Ops leadership have full access. Hiring managers and panelists have access to records they own. Engineering and product leadership may request de-identified aggregates.
- Legal holds: If a legal hold is placed, the record remains in active secure storage until release by Legal.

Debiasing measures (operationalized)
- Automated blind-aggregation: The system computes an anonymous panel variance score. If variance > 1.25 (on a 5-point rubric), the Debiasing Checkpoint triggers.
- Anonymized review packets: For checkpoints, People Ops prepares a packet with redacted candidate identifiers and a neutral summary of strengths/risks. Reviewers are asked to focus on evidence only.
- Structured counterfactual prompts: During calibration calls we use three standard prompts to surface bias: 1) Would we hire if this candidate had a different background? 2) Which criteria most influenced the negative signal? 3) Could a reasonable accommodation or role adjustment change outcome?
- Bias incident logging: Any concern raised during checkpoint is logged as an incident with a tag (e.g., gender-bias, halo-effect, cultural-fit). People Ops maintains a quarterly register of incidents and remediation actions.

Calibration and audit cadence
- Weekly lightweight review: People Ops inspects records flagged by automation (debiasing_flag or high variance) and triages for calibration.
- Quarterly calibration: Cross-functional hiring committee meets to review a statistically representative sample (n >= 30 records) focusing on equity metrics and rubric drift. Deliverable: a calibration memo and recommended rubric updates.
- Annual audit: People Ops and Legal run an annual audit against retention policy, redaction compliance, and adverse impact metrics. Legal receives a copy of the audit report.

Operational integrations and automations
- ATS (Greenhouse): canonical source of scorecards and interview scheduling. Integration extracts score_summary and scorecard id on submit.
- HRIS (Workday): post-hire writes a Workday placeholder (not PII) to the decision record to support onboarding workflows.
- Artifact store (S3 encrypted): technical exercises and code tests are stored with hashed filenames; archive contains links only.
- Slack workflow: /archive-decision command opens the Confluence form pre-populated from ATS record.
- Retention job: nightly lambda moves expired records to cold storage and updates the Confluence metadata.

Manager and panel owner responsibilities (quick reference)
1. Ensure rubrics and evaluation artifacts are complete before final submit.
2. Redact PII from notes per redaction rules.
3. Flag Debiasing Checkpoint when required.
4. Respond to calibration requests promptly (<= 5 business days).

When to escalate to People Ops or Legal
- Candidate or hiring manager alleges discrimination or inconsistent process.
- Legal hold is requested.
- Evidence contains potential PII leakage or third-party IP concerns in assignments.

Metrics to track (examples)
- Time-to-decision (median days between final interview and decision archive submit)
- Redaction compliance rate (target > 98%)
- Debiasing checkpoint frequency and resolution outcomes
- Panel variance distribution by role seniority
- Adverse impact measures by demographic group (People Ops / Legal only)

Templates and artifacts (links)
- Decision record form: /confluence/people-ops/forms/hiring-decision-record
- Redaction checklist: /confluence/people-ops/redaction-checklist-v1.0
- Calibration memo template: /confluence/people-ops/calibration-memo-template

Appendix A — Redaction quick rules
- Remove direct contact data (email, phone, address).
- Remove medical/disability information unless candidate has explicitly discussed accommodations relevant to role (then consult People Ops).
- Replace names with initials or role-based placeholders (e.g., Candidate-1).

Appendix B — Example decision narrative (good)
Primary rationale:
Candidate demonstrated consistent systems knowledge and clear ownership examples. The coding exercise fell short of the rubric threshold primarily in algorithmic optimization (two-timeouts on hidden tests). We propose passing only if candidate is offered a level-rebalanced role focused on software reliability and given a 12-week ramp with a targeted mentorship plan. Evidence: code-test v2.1 (link), interview notes (redacted link).

Appendix C — Frequently asked questions
Q: Who can see the unredacted record?
A: People Ops and Legal have access to unredacted records stored in the secure artifact store. Panel members see redacted views in Confluence.

Q: What if a hiring manager disagrees with People Ops during a debiasing checkpoint?
A: The calibration meeting is advisory. If disagreement persists, escalate to the cross-functional hiring committee for a final decision within 10 business days.

Contact
People Ops hiring systems: people-ops@redwood.ai | Slack: @peopleops. For Legal escalation: legal@redwood.ai.
